about.title: Personal Injury Help in Danville, California
about.longDescription: Danville sits along a busy stretch of the I-680 corridor, where traffic moving through Contra Costa County mixes with local drivers heading to Camino Tassajara and nearby neighborhoods. In the most recent full year on record, Danville saw 102 injury collisions and 134 people hurt, with one traffic death — numbers that reflect how much of daily life here happens on and around these same roads. Crashes tend to cluster on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., a pattern consistent with commuter and school-pickup traffic converging at once. If you or someone you love was injured in one of these incidents, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and paperwork can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. We handle personal injury claims in Danville and work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money on your behalf. Reaching out costs nothing and doesn't commit you to anything.

whyChoose.title: What Danville Residents Should Know About California Injury Law

items.title: Your Filing Window Is Limited
items.desc: California generally gives injury victims two years from the date of the accident to file a claim, but claims against a government entity — like a city road issue — can require notice in as little as six months. Acting sooner protects your options.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still pursue compensation — it's simply reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering Claims
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in standard personal injury cases.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if we recover money for you. There's no retainer and no hourly billing to worry about.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Danville?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity was involved, such as a road maintained by a public agency, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking your timeline promptly.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Danville?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along I-680, including both the northbound and southbound directions, as well as Camino Tassajara. These are simply the corridors with the most recorded incidents, not a judgment about any specific location.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so partial fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would just be reduced in proportion to your share of responsibility.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency — meaning we only collect a fee if we win or settle your case. There's no cost or obligation to reach out.

items.question: Do you represent clients directly?
items.answer: Yes. We handle personal injury claims in Danville and work directly with our clients. We work with you directly and represent your interests throughout your case.
